summary.intent: Ship phase 68.1 (web client runtime integration) for the cipher-box repo: push the 6 subsystem commits, open PR #588, extract phase learnings, and get all CI checks green before merge.
summary.outcome: PR #588 was pushed and opened; CodeRabbit skipped review (file-count limit) but Greptile passed; a stale apps/api test (shares.controller.spec.ts) was found causing the CI 'Test' job to fail, root-caused, and fixed with a verified local test run; learnings were captured in 68.1-LEARNINGS.md; sdk-core/sdk coverage gates were being verified locally and the api spec fix committed as the session transcript ends.

repo: CodeRabbit skips PR-level review entirely when a PR touches more than 150 files (hit at 207 files) — must run CodeRabbit directory-scoped locally beforehand to still get its findings.

CI's Test job runs apps/api, sdk-core, sdk, and crypto coverage steps sequentially; if the API step fails, CI skips the later sdk-core/sdk/crypto coverage steps entirely, hiding whether those gates pass.

sharesService.updateGrant takes 6 args (added writeDescriptorRef?, clearWriteDescriptor? for write-grant support in phase 68.1); a stale spec still asserted only 4 args, causing a CI-only failure not caught by local `test` runs (CI uses `test:coverage` with gates).
After PR creation, the release bot pushes a chore(release) commit — always fetch+rebase before any further push to avoid clobbering it.

code.finding: updateGrant test assertion expected sharesService.updateGrant called with 4 args; controller actually calls it with 6 (including writeDescriptorRef, clearWriteDescriptor forwarded as undefined when DTO omits them). Fixed by updating the assertion to include the 2 trailing undefined args.
Correctly passes 6 args to sharesService.updateGrant including writeDescriptorRef and clearWriteDescriptor, which are real DTO fields added for write-grant support this phase.
updateGrant signature takes 6 params (writeDescriptorRef?, clearWriteDescriptor? added), confirming production code was correct and the spec was the stale side.

workflow: When a CI job fails, drill down via job step list -> targeted log tail for the specific failing step rather than dumping the whole job log (avoids noise from unrelated negative-path test ERRORs).
Run coverage-gated test suites locally before pushing a fix to avoid an extra CI round-trip, especially when later coverage steps were skipped due to an earlier step's failure.
Background-poll for slow, non-deterministic CI/bot state (Greptile review, release bot push) while a learnings-extraction agent runs in parallel, to avoid blocking on either.

friction: Initial `git push` hit a connection timeout despite fetch/gh working moments earlier — required a retry (likely transient network blip).

The backgrounded check poll ('Poll until Greptile and Release Preview settle') failed with exit code 1, apparently a transient `gh` blip, requiring a manual re-check of PR state instead of relying on the poll's output.
CodeRabbit's 150-file PR review cap meant its automated review was skipped entirely on this large PR, necessitating the earlier local directory-scoped run as a workaround.
CI's Test job failing on apps/api caused later sdk-core/sdk/crypto coverage steps to be skipped, leaving their pass/fail status unknown until run locally.
`--log-failed` on the gh CLI dumped the entire job log rather than isolating the failing step, requiring extra steps to pinpoint the actual failure.
open_items: Confirm sdk-core and sdk coverage gates pass locally (deleted dead code in sdk-core and added new code in both) before pushing again.
Commit the apps/api spec fix and push, after fetching/rebasing over the release bot's chore(release) commit.
Resolve any Greptile review threads on PR #588 before final push/merge.
Confirm full CI check set is green on PR #588 before handing off the merge decision.
